titel: Robby Hoffman thinks comics can ‘say anything’ — and she does

einzeiler: Comedian Robbie Hoffman on jokes, controversy, and her unconventional path to success
kurzfassung: Comedian Robbie Hoffman discusses her journey from poverty and a strict upbringing to comedy success. She reflects on handling public criticism, her views on what comics can say, and a memorable clash at a Writers Guild meeting. Hoffman also shares her thoughts on money, family perseverance, and navigating sensitive topics through humor.
stichpunkte: Reflects on her brutal first stand-up set in a sketchy Canadian loft where she briefly fainted from nerves and smoke
Discusses why she does not take personal responsibility for how audiences interpret her provocative jokes, such as material about pedophilia
Recalls a turbulent meeting with the Writers Guild of America where she questioned board salaries and real estate holdings
Credits her mother's persistent, step-by-step approach to earning a university degree over 12 years as a major influence on her own tenacity
Describes her complicated relationship with money, having grown up poor and now deeply appreciating financial security while remaining anxious about losing it
Defends her right to joke about queer and non-binary topics as a member of the community who processes life through humor
Expresses interest in hosting a late-night television show despite acknowledging her inability to read a teleprompter smoothly

clips.hook: Fainting during a first comedy set
clips.text: The comedian recalls experiencing dizziness, nausea, and blacking out during her very first time performing stand-up in a makeshift comedy venue.
Reflecting on her upbringing, the speaker admits that societal marketing around wealth worked on her and she genuinely enjoys having money.

clips.hook: Being silenced at a union meeting
clips.text: She describes feeling scolded like a child and reduced to tears when a board member publicly told her to sit down during a professional guild gathering.

clips.hook: Who has the right to joke about queer topics
clips.text: Arguing from her own lived experience in the queer community, she asserts that she should be allowed to explore these topics through comedy more than outsiders can.

beschreibung:
There’s a gripe in the comedy scene these days that ‘you can’t say anything anymore.’ Robby Hoffman doesn’t buy it.

“Bro, you just did,” she says, responding to an ‘old guard’ of comics who feel maligned for speaking their mind. “You could say anything. But other people had a reaction to it. That also can happen.”

Hoffman, for her part, has a lot to say — and more opportunities than ever to do so, from scene-stealing roles in Emmy-nominated shows like Hacks to her most recent Netflix special, Wake Up.

She also doesn’t shy away from criticism for what she said in that special, including lengthy jokes about the non-binary community and dismissing the use of they/them pronouns.

Hoffman, who describes herself as “somebody who’s clearly in the queer space, who cut my tits off, who could be they/them at the drop of a hat,” pushes back on critics who suggest that her jokes about the topic could be dangerous.

“I like to cope and explore through jokes, and I feel like. I should be more able to do that than, say, some of my counterparts,” Hoffman says. “I feel like if I can’t talk about it, who can?”

In this episode of Newsmakers, NPR’s Juana Summers sat down with Robby Hoffman at The Comedy Store in Los Angeles to discuss her journey to success and what’s next in her career.

“So much, I can’t talk about it,” she says. “I don’t want to jinx it.”
